## Engine

Deterministic: yes, two generations of the same input are identical (deep-equal).

### Generation time, one month (2026-12, 32 employees, 34 brand-processes)

Median of 10 runs after one discarded warm-up. The previous month is generated in memory first for the boundary week, and not timed.

| Run | Median | Min | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generate + validate + ranked suggestions (what the Generate button runs) | 340 ms | 335 ms | 358 ms |
| Generate + validate, no suggestions | 59.1 ms | 58.3 ms | 63.0 ms |

### Scaling: synthetic copies of the whole organisation

Each copy adds its own pods, people, brands, assignments and leaves, and shares the calendar and process catalog. Median of 10 runs (1x, 2x), 5 runs (4x); with suggestions, median of 5 (3 at 4x). Engine only, no database or network.

| Scale | Employees | Brand-processes | Roster cells | Generate + validate | Same, with suggestions | vs 1x (no suggestions) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1x | 32 | 34 | 1120 | 58.6 ms | 329 ms | 1.0x |
| 2x | 64 | 68 | 2240 | 181 ms | 1853 ms | 3.1x |
| 4x | 128 | 136 | 4480 | 637 ms | 12372 ms | 10.9x |

## Coverage of the seeded demand

A demand-day is one brand-process on one day it must be staffed (operating rule, holidays, weekday minimums and overrides applied), over 2026-12 and 2027-01. It is covered when at least the required number of people work it. The roster is the engine's own output; nothing is edited by hand.

| Scenario | Demand-days | Covered | ERROR issues |
|---|---|---|---|
| With backups (as seeded) | 1850 | 1850 (100.0%) | 9 |
| Without backups (all 24 BACKUP assignments removed, regenerated) | 1850 | 1793 (96.9%) | 112 |

ERROR issues by code. Coverage alone can flatter: the engine keeps a person working rather than open a coverage gap, and then reports the missing weekly off as an ERROR.

| ERROR code | With backups | Without backups |
|---|---|---|
| `WEEKLY_OFF_NOT_GRANTED` | 9 | 54 |
| `COVERAGE_GAP` | 0 | 57 |
| `CASCADE_GAP` | 0 | 1 |

Removing the backups leaves 57 more demand-days short and raises the ERROR count from 9 to 112.

## Weekly-off fairness (a known weakness)

Generated the way the live app does on a fresh database: December first, then January with the December draft as its neighbour. Eligible = assigned to a brand-process that operates on at least one non-holiday Sunday of the month.

| Month | Sundays | Eligible people | No weekly off on a Sunday | Worked every Sunday | Sundays worked, min to max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-12 | 3 | 26 | 15 (57.7%) | 15 | 0 to 3 |
| 2027-01 | 5 | 26 | 20 (76.9%) | 20 | 0 to 5 |

Most weekly offs land on weekdays, where coverage is easiest to keep. The engine does not yet spread Sundays evenly. The fairness report page shows the same numbers per person.

## Issue codes

The validator defines 12 issue codes (7 ERROR, 4 WARNING, 1 INFO).
5 of 12 appear on the baseline seed rosters; 12 of 12 are referenced by name in the engine or server tests.

| Code | Severity | On the baseline seed | Named in tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `COVERAGE_GAP` | ERROR | - | yes |
| `NO_ELIGIBLE_STAFF` | ERROR | - | yes |
| `WORK_WHILE_UNAVAILABLE` | ERROR | - | yes |
| `WEEKLY_OFF_NOT_GRANTED` | ERROR | 9 | yes |
| `FIXED_OFF_VIOLATED` | ERROR | - | yes |
| `SHIFT_INCOMPATIBLE` | ERROR | - | yes |
| `OVERALLOCATED` | WARNING | - | yes |
| `CASCADE_GAP` | ERROR | - | yes |
| `PREFERRED_OFF_NOT_HONOURED` | WARNING | 18 | yes |
| `CONSECUTIVE_DAYS_EXCEEDED` | WARNING | 3 | yes |
| `PENDING_LEAVE_CONFLICT` | WARNING | 2 | yes |
| `COMP_OFF_EARNED` | INFO | 40 | yes |

Codes that do not appear on the baseline appear when the demo changes something (a manual edit, a what-if leave, a rule change). That is by design: the baseline is built to fail only where the demo scenarios say.
